Statistical Analysis¶

neurora.stats_cal

Function Index¶

  • stats

  • stats_fmri

  • stats_iscfmri

API Details¶

a module for conducting the statistical analysis

neurora.stats_cal.stats(corrs, alternative='greater')¶

Conduct statistical analysis for EEG-like correlation results.

Parameters:

  • corrs (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_chls, n_ts]) –

    Correlation coefficients.

    n_subs, n_chls, and n_ts represent the number of subjects, channels, and time points, respectively.

  • alternative ({"two-sided", "less", "greater"}, default="greater") – Alternative hypothesis for one-sample t-tests against zero.

Returns:

stat_results – Statistical results.

The last dimension contains:

  • stat_results[…, 0] : t-value

  • stat_results[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_chls, n_ts, 2]

Notes

n_subs must be at least 6.

Fisher z transformation is always applied before the t-test.

This function can be used for subject-level EEG-like correlation results, such as NPS, ISC summaries, or EEG-like RDM correlations.

neurora.stats_cal.stats_fmri(corrs, alternative='greater')¶

Conduct statistical analysis for fMRI searchlight correlation results.

Parameters:

  • corrs (array_like, shape [n_subs, n_x, n_y, n_z]) –

    Correlation coefficients.

    n_subs, n_x, n_y, and n_z represent the number of subjects and searchlight units along the x, y, and z axes.

  • alternative ({"two-sided", "less", "greater"}, default="greater") – Alternative hypothesis for one-sample t-tests against zero.

Returns:

stat_results – Statistical results.

The last dimension contains:

  • stat_results[…, 0] : t-value

  • stat_results[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_x, n_y, n_z, 2]

Notes

n_subs must be at least 6.

Fisher z transformation is always applied before the t-test.

This function can be used for subject-level fMRI searchlight results, such as searchlight NPS or searchlight RDM correlations.

neurora.stats_cal.stats_iscfmri(corrs, alternative='greater')¶

Conduct statistical analysis for fMRI ISC searchlight results.

Parameters:

  • corrs (array_like, shape [n_ts, n_pairs, n_x, n_y, n_z]) –

    ISC correlation coefficients.

    n_ts, n_pairs, n_x, n_y, and n_z represent the number of time points, subject pairs, and searchlight units along the x, y, and z axes.

  • alternative ({"two-sided", "less", "greater"}, default="greater") – Alternative hypothesis for one-sample t-tests against zero.

Returns:

stat_results – Statistical results.

The last dimension contains:

  • stat_results[…, 0] : t-value

  • stat_results[…, 1] : p-value

Return type:

ndarray, shape [n_ts, n_x, n_y, n_z, 2]

Notes

n_pairs must be at least 6.

Fisher z transformation is always applied before the t-test.

The second dimension of corrs is the subject-pair dimension. This function performs one-sample t-tests across subject pairs.
